source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading: This Flexential facility is in one of the company national markets confirmed on its own homepage covering Oregon (Portland/Hillsboro), Texas (Dallas, Plano, Richardson), Ohio (West Chester, Cincinnati market), Kentucky (Louisville), Pennsylvania (Allentown, Collegeville, Philadelphia market), Virginia (Richmond), Minnesota (Chaska, Minneapolis market), and Arizona (Phoenix). Flexential was formed from the 2017 merger of ViaWest, founded 1999, and Peak 10, founded 2000, followed by a 2018 rebrand to Flexential. The company reports 40 plus data centers across 18 national markets, 3 million plus square feet of facilities, an 800 million dollar expansion investment, and a planned new campus on 110 acres in Kaufman County near Dallas. This specific state cluster was confirmed as an active Flexential market on the company own site, but no market specific founding, acquisition, or building history distinct from the general ViaWest and Peak 10 company story was located in available sourcing this session.

reading.body:
At 5.3 MW of published IT capacity, Flexential Portland – Hillsboro 1 is a mid-sized colocation facility by any current AI-infrastructure standard. Assuming 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 5.3 MW supports roughly 132 racks (5,300 kW ÷ 40 kW = 132.5). At a more conservative enterprise average of 10 kW per rack, that same power budget fills about 530 racks. Either way, the campus sits well below the threshold, typically cited as tens or hundreds of megawatts, where a single site becomes meaningful to hyperscale AI training at scale. The 85,388 square feet of technical space suggests the building is not power-dense by modern GPU-cluster standards, because 5.3 MW across that footprint averages roughly 62 watts per square foot, a figure consistent with mixed enterprise workloads rather than purpose-built AI infrastructure.

The certification stack qualifies this campus to host regulated and sensitive workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls. PCI DSS qualifies it for cardholder data environments. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense and aerospace data. NIST 800-53 and HITRUST together cover federal-adjacent and healthcare data. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard underlying the SOC reports rather than a separate compliance regime. Which tenants occupy the facility is not published.

Within Oregon, this campus ranks seventh out of the eight facilities for which this site has read a published megawatt figure, out of 133 total mapped facilities in the state. Its 5.3 MW represents roughly 2.8 percent of the 192.6 MW published across those eight Oregon sites (5.3 ÷ 192.6 = 0.028). Because only eight of 133 mapped Oregon facilities publish any capacity figure, the state total is almost certainly an undercount, and this campus's true share of Oregon capacity is likely smaller still. For an operator or researcher sizing AI infrastructure in the Pacific Northwest, this site is a secondary node, suited to regulated enterprise workloads, not a primary destination for large-scale model training.
